own_solution.law: For reversible operation, dW=(1-290/T)dQ and dQ=-mc dT. Thus W_max=mc integral from 290 K to 360 K of (1-290/T)dT=mc[70-290 ln(360/290)].
assumptions: The water has a uniform temperature throughout reversible cooling.
The tank's heat capacity is negligible under the standard idealization of the apparatus.
The engine is cyclic, and heat exchange occurs only with the water and the constant-temperature lake.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TC03C and T557D replace the specified 1.4 kg with an unspecified 'small amount', violating the requirement that variants preserve the same number and unit.

notes: The base physics and numerical answer are well posed. Both additions to the operating tank increase its water mass to 3.4 kg. Water present only in an earlier experiment, or placed in the unconnected second tank, has no physical path to the target. TE3D6/TC03C and T24C4/T557D fail the stated numerical matching requirement, although those differences do not change the work.
